g.text: The OsHandler thread waits for any child of the Launch
Manager. It only learns the PID and an exit status,
not which component the process belongs to.
look up the component for the PID
The lookup removes the entry that was added when the
component registered its process - see Component Activation.
notify the component of the termination
[the exit is not an expected completion]
Of a component that has finished starting, only a self
terminating one that exits with status 0 is a completion.
Every other exit is an unexpected termination.
[the component is self terminating and exited with status 0]
[an activation is waiting for exactly this termination]
The ready condition of the component is its own
termination: the exit releases the waiting worker, and
that worker reports the successful activation - see
[the component became ready before it exited]
The expected exit of an already ready component is not
an event: the graph keeps the component as activated.
[the termination was requested or the component is still starting]
The worker that is waiting inside the activation or the
deactivation is released instead, and that worker reports
An unexpected termination always leaves the active Run Target.
The clean up is done in place on the main loop thread, not on

the graph moves to kUndefinedState right away
The graph moves to kAborting and stays there until the last

In kUndefinedState and without a pending request from outside,
the main loop starts a transition to the fallback Run Target.
start a transition to the fallback Run Target
From here the recovery runs as an ordinary transition
- see Component Deactivation and Component Activation.
The whole notification path runs on the OsHandler thread; the graph only ever
reacts to the resulting event on the main loop thread.
